Figure 1: Static analysis of StealC malware.

Figure 6: This figures illustrate the workflow example of ABLE on a StealC malware. Stage 1: Baseline execution detects only 7 generic signatures without family attribution; the LLM analyzes the trace and identifies time-based evasion logic. Stage 2: Iteration 0 attempts to bypass variable comparisons but fails. Iteration 1 targets absolute calls (FF 15) near the exit point; the debugger log shows breakpoints hit but evasion remains intact. Stage 3: The LLM suggests targeting relative calls (E8) instead, hypothesizing these invoke internal evasion-checking functions. Iteration 2 adopts this strategy, revealing 4 hidden behaviors including C2 communication (162.0.238.10) and correctly identifying the sample as StealC.
